title: Lot Genealogy
brief: A customer of Meridian Microworks reports thickness out of limit on wafers from shipped lot {{lot}}. You need to trace the lot genealogy: which child lots, tools, and gauges were involved, and what else is affected. You have 12 visit points.

actions.label: General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.label: Older records for this area
actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

actions.label: Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: Lot history for {{lot}} shows polisher P-2, gauge TG-5, and a split into child lots {{lot}}.1 and {{lot}}.2.
evidence.whyItMatters: Genealogy records link the lot to tools and instruments.
evidence.missedExplanation: This record is the map for the trail.

evidence.text: Split record: child lot {{lot}}.2 was merged with lot L-7790 for shipping; the merged carrier carries only the L-7790 number.
evidence.whyItMatters: Identity must be kept through merges; otherwise affected wafers ship under another lot.
evidence.missedExplanation: Follow every child lot to its end.

evidence.text: Gauge TG-5 failed its calibration 2 days after measuring {{lot}}; it read 0.8 micrometers low. No review of earlier results is recorded.
evidence.whyItMatters: When an instrument is found out of tolerance, the validity of earlier results must be assessed.
evidence.missedExplanation: Check calibration results after the lot date, not only before.

evidence.text: Measurement data shows {{lot}} passed at 0.3 micrometers inside the upper limit.
evidence.whyItMatters: The lot passed as measured; the gauge error explains the escape.

evidence.text: Polisher P-2 tool log shows a pad change was overdue by 140 wafers when {{lot}} ran.
evidence.whyItMatters: Controlled conditions include defined consumable changes.
evidence.missedExplanation: Compare consumable intervals with actual use.

evidence.text: Pad change record form PC-2 does not show wafer count at the change, so intervals are calculated by hand.
evidence.whyItMatters: Recording the count would make the control visible.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask how the interval is known.

evidence.text: Shipping records show child lot {{lot}}.1 and merged lot L-7790 went to 2 different customers.
evidence.whyItMatters: The organization must know where affected output went.
evidence.missedExplanation: Trace shipments for every child lot.

evidence.text: Hold record H-219 places all remaining {{lot}} material on hold as of today.
Customer-supplied wafer register for the customer is current.
Engineer: "Rework lots get a B suffix, but some technicians use .R instead." 2 naming styles found in week 30.
evidence.missedExplanation: Ask how special lots are named.

evidence.text: Box labels show lot number, quantity, and date in the defined format.

decisions.prompt: What is the scope of containment and review?
options: {{lot}} and both child lots, merged lot L-7790, and every lot measured on TG-5 since its last good calibration
All wafers ever polished on P-2
decisions.rationale: The merge, the gauge error, and the shipments each widen the scope.

containment: Hold remaining material and notify both customers; review all lots measured on TG-5 since its last good calibration
correction: Re-measure held wafers with a verified gauge and disposition as authorized
cause: Merges do not preserve child lot identity, gauge failures do not trigger a review of earlier results, and pad changes are not counted
corrective: Block merges that drop lot identity; add an automatic look-back on failed calibration; record wafer count at pad changes
effectiveness: Audit merge records and calibration look-backs for three months

debriefText.found: You traced the genealogy through splits, merges, and the gauge.
debriefText.missed: The most-missed card is the gauge failing calibration after the lot ran.
debriefText.falseFinding: Correct labels and formatting are not problems.
